chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, who said:
I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Does the woman dye (her hair) while she is menstruating?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim (title of the 7th Imam, Musa al-Kazim)

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman dye her hair with henna?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that a menstruating woman may dye her hair, clarifying that the state of *hadath akbar* (major ritual impurity) does not restrict acts of adornment or preparation for purity. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between restrictions on prayer and Quran recitation versus permissible personal grooming, emphasizing that menstruation is a natural state rather than a state of ceremonial impurity (*najis*) that blocks all activities. The brevity of the report highlights the straightforward nature of this specific fiqh issue within the broader context of women's ritual status.
